handoff.purpose: Enforces allocation and containment policy for worktree creation, deletion, and branch reaping.

symbols.name: _require_allocated_worktree
symbols.note: Validates path is an allocated worktree via lexical, no-follow, and identity checks.

symbols.name: create_worktree
symbols.note: Creates a git worktree after containment checks and records allocation.

symbols.name: cleanup_worktree
symbols.note: Removes an allocated worktree directory and deregisters it, retaining the record.

symbols.name: reap_branches
symbols.note: Deletes candidate branches that provably hold no work (method body not in this chunk).

claims.text: Ordering is the whole defect being fixed, so it is spelled out: every check below is lexical or no-follow, and the returned path is the UNRESOLVED one -- callers operate on exactly what was checked.
claims.why: The method returns `target` as `_lexical(Path(path))` (line 846) and all checks from steps 1-6 use lexical or no-follow operations (e.g., `_is_reparse_point`, `_lexists`, `os.lstat`). The only resolution is in step 4, but the returned path remains unresolved.

claims.text: 1. inside the manager's own root, and never the root itself.
claims.why: Line 849 checks `_key(target) == _key(root) or not _is_within(target, root)` and raises if so.

claims.text: 2. never the primary checkout, an ancestor of it, or anything in it.
claims.why: Line 853 calls `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(target, "path")` which implements this check (though the implementation is elsewhere).

claims.text: 3. no symlink / junction anywhere from the worktree root down. Checked top-down and BEFORE any resolution: a reparse point at any level can redirect everything below it.
claims.why: Lines 857-861 iterate `_reach_chain(target)` and raise on `_is_reparse_point(component)`. The chain is built from root down, and it occurs before resolution in step 4.

claims.text: 4. only now is resolution trustworthy -- nothing at or below the root can redirect it. Re-check the repo relation on the resolved form so a root that itself sits under a symlinked prefix cannot smuggle the target back into the checkout.
claims.why: Lines 864-874 resolve both target and root, then call `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(resolved, "resolved path")` and check containment with `_is_within(resolved, resolved_root)`.

claims.text: 5. it must actually be there, as a real directory (no-follow).
claims.why: Lines 876-881 check `_lexists(target)` and `stat.S_ISDIR(os.lstat(target).st_mode)`.

claims.text: 6. it must be something THIS manager allocated for THIS repo.
claims.why: Line 884 calls `_read_allocation(target)` and raises if None.

claims.text: WorktreeContainmentError: If the requested placement escapes the manager's worktree root or touches the primary checkout.
claims.why: Lines 900-903 raise WorktreeContainmentError for escape; `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` raises the same for touching the primary checkout (though the exact exception type for the latter is not shown).

claims.text: StorageUnavailable: If the worktree root volume is missing or below the free-space watermark (fail-closed; never spills elsewhere).
claims.why: The `require_storage` call on line 908 could raise this, but the exception type is defined elsewhere; the chunk does not show its implementation.

claims.text: ORDER IS DELIBERATE, and it is what makes each of these testable on its own. "Is this inside the developer's checkout?" is the worst answer, so it is asked FIRST and named precisely; asking it after the escape check would make it unreachable, because a path that escapes the root INTO the checkout would already have been refused with the generic reason.
claims.why: Line 892 calls `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(worktree_path, "allocation path")` before the escape check on lines 893-897, matching the stated order.

claims.text: WHAT IS NOT HERE, and why. There used to be a second lexical call, `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(_lexical(root), "worktree root")`. It is DOMINATED -- 0 counterexamples in 216,225 enumerated (root, repo, branch) shapes -- but NOT for the reason an earlier version of this comment gave. That version claimed the allocation-path check on the line below covers everything the root check did. It does not: with the RESOLVED-root check disabled, 955 of those shapes survive, every one of the form "the root is a strict ANCESTOR of the checkout and the allocation path is a sibling of it" (root C:/a, repo C:/a/a, branch tb). The allocation path in those is repo-adjacent to nothing, so the line below stays silent. What actually covers them is the RESOLVED-root check further down: on a genuine ancestor chain with no reparse points, realpath is the identity map, so the resolved root is still that strict ancestor and `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` fires on it. The removed guard is dominated by the pair, not by the allocation path alone -- and its replacement is not dominated in return, because it also catches the case the whole lexical pair was blind to (a junction inside DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT).
claims.why: The code currently calls `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(worktree_path, "allocation path")` (line 892), checks containment (lines 893-897), resolves the root (lines 906-907) and calls `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(resolved_root, "resolved worktree root")` (line 908). There is no second lexical root call. The reasoning about the resolved-root check covering the ancestor case is consistent with the code flow.

claims.text: Identity first: a directory that exists without a record is a directory nothing is allowed to delete.
claims.why: Line 911 calls `_record_allocation(worktree_path, branch_name)` before creating the worktree via `_run_git` on line 913.

claims.text: Pin the branch tip as created. Later this is the ONLY thing that can prove a candidate branch holds no work -- a sha comparison, not a heuristic and not a locale-dependent message from `git branch -d`.
claims.why: Lines 916-917 run `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/{branch_name}` and store the result via `_record_allocation`. This is a sha comparison, not a heuristic.

claims.text: The in-memory twin of the record. This, not the file, is what may later authorise deleting a branch.
claims.why: Lines 921-927 store the allocation in `self._allocations` with `branch_tip_at_creation` and `worktree_removed: False`.

claims.text: The target must be PROVEN to be a worktree this manager allocated (see :meth:`_require_allocated_worktree`); anything else raises without removing a thing.
claims.why: Line 938 calls `self._require_allocated_worktree(path)` which raises on any failure before removal.

claims.text: The removal itself is done here rather than by ``git worktree remove --force``, which follows reparse points planted inside the tree; ``git worktree prune`` then deregisters it.
claims.why: Lines 946-952 call `_remove_tree_no_follow` (which does not follow reparse points) and line 957 runs `git worktree prune`.

claims.text: The candidate BRANCH is deliberately left alone here -- see :meth:`reap_branches` for why deleting it in this call would be wrong.
claims.why: The method never touches the branch; it only removes the directory and prunes. The rationale is in reap_branches (not in this chunk).

claims.text: WorktreeContainmentError: If the target cannot be proven to be an allocated worktree, or if the primary checkout is no longer the directory this manager was created for. Nothing is removed in either case.
claims.why: Lines 936-937 call `_refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved()` which raises before removal; `_require_allocated_worktree` raises WorktreeContainmentError if not proven. Nothing is removed before these checks.

claims.text: WorktreeRemovalRace: If a reparse point appeared above the removal while it was underway. The tree is PARTIALLY removed and that is what the exception says; it is deliberately not repaired.
claims.why: The comment on lines 953-955 states WorktreeRemovalRace is a RuntimeError that passes through undisguised, implying partial removal and no repair. The exception is not caught or repaired here.

claims.text: RuntimeError: If the worktree directory could not be removed. A failed removal is never swallowed silently.
claims.why: Lines 948-950 catch OSError and raise RuntimeError with the message.

claims.text: Asked FIRST, before the target is even examined: if the primary checkout has moved, nothing this method could prove about the target is worth acting on. See the method for what this does and does not cover -- it is a mitigation for the move-in attack, not a closure.
claims.why: Line 936 calls `_refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved()` before `_require_allocated_worktree` on line 938.

claims.text: Everything above the target that the removal will read the tree THROUGH. Step 3 already checked this chain; the walk re-checks it on every directory it opens, because a check that happened earlier is not a check that holds now.
claims.why: Line 944 computes `guarded = self._reach_chain(target)[:-1]` and passes it to `_remove_tree_no_follow` on line 945, which re-checks ancestors.

claims.text: WorktreeRemovalRace is a RuntimeError, not an OSError: it passes through undisguised so a caller can tell "nothing happened" from "this was attacked halfway".
claims.why: The except clause on line 946 catches only OSError; WorktreeRemovalRace is not caught, so it propagates.

claims.text: The directory is gone; deregister it. A prune failure raises (RuntimeError from _run_git) rather than leaving a stale registration unreported.
claims.why: Line 957 calls `self._run_git('worktree', 'prune')` which, per the comment, raises RuntimeError on failure. No try/except swallows it.

claims.text: The record is RETAINED, not discarded: it is now the only place that remembers which branch this worktree left behind and what its tip was at creation, which is what makes a later reap safe. The retained record can never re-authorise a delete -- cleanup refuses a path that does not exist, and this one no longer does.
claims.why: Lines 960-961 update the record with `worktree_removed_ts` and write it via `_write_allocation`, not discard it. Since the path no longer exists, `_require_allocated_worktree` would refuse it.

claims.text: Tracked in memory as well as on disk: reap must not be steerable into deleting the branch of a worktree that is still LIVE just because a candidate wrote a `worktree_removed_ts` into its record.
claims.why: Lines 963-966 set `allocation["worktree_removed"] = True` in `self._allocations` after checking the in-memory allocation exists.

claims.text: Delete candidate branches that provably hold no work. Explicit step. WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF ``cleanup_worktree``
claims.why: The method body and the full rationale are not in this chunk.

observations.what: The `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` call in `create_worktree` is placed before the containment check, as documented. However, the exact exception type raised by `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` is not shown; the docstring claims WorktreeContainmentError, but the function might raise a different type.

The `_refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved` method is called with no arguments in `cleanup_worktree`, but its implementation (which likely uses `self.repo_path` and `self._repo_identity`) is not in this chunk; the claim that it checks the primary checkout is unverified here.

The `_read_allocation` call in `_require_allocated_worktree` returns None for a missing record, but the function might also return a dict with a 'worktree_removed' flag; the chunk does not show how a record with `worktree_removed=True` is treated, so the claim that a removed worktree cannot be re-authorised is only partially verified.
The `reap_branches` method is only declared and its docstring is truncated; the claim that it is separate from cleanup_worktree is uncheckable here.
